minors.title: consumed.json's referenced-fires sha1 call doesn't guard the same None case its own n_rows fallback anticipates
minors.detail: In eval/utils/probe_eval.py's run(), the generator branch computes `ref_fires_height = ref[1].height if ref[1] is not None else 0` (correctly anticipating that read_report can return None for the fires frame per its own documented contract: "returns None for the frame when no fires.parquet exists"), but the very next line unconditionally calls `_sha1(ref_eval_dir / "fires.parquet")`, which would raise FileNotFoundError instead of falling back gracefully if that file were ever absent. In practice this is unreachable today because every classifier method (2.6) must return a non-None fires frame from report(), so ctool.py's referenced reports always have fires.parquet on disk — but the inconsistency between the two adjacent lines (one guards the None case, the other doesn't) is worth tidying since it is easy to miss if a future classifier method's report() is written differently.

minors.title: Heartbeat emission order deviates from the ticket's literal step 6 placement
minors.detail: Ticket step 6 places `hb.emit(0, len(pairs), "row")` then 'one beat per record read' before steps 7-8 (resolving split files, split gates), while step 9 places the actual `trajectory_record.read_dir` call after those same gates. Since `read_dir` offers no per-record callback, the two placements can't both be honored literally (the implementer's report documents this contradiction explicitly). The code emits the initial beat at step 6's position, then emits `len(pairs)` per-record beats immediately after the single `read_dir` call (step 9's position) rather than truly interleaved with disk reads. This doesn't change any observable output (verified against `heartbeat/0-0.jsonl` in F2's acceptance output) and is explained by a code comment plus the report's 'Decisions I made' section.

minors.title: Round-trip gate checked once per event rather than once per row
minors.detail: Ticket step 14 lists the call round-trip check among the 'row gates,' implying it applies per built row (per cut), but the code checks it once per event, before the cut/offset loop runs (since `tool`/`call`/`args` are identical across all cuts of one event, a failure would fire identically for every row of that event). The error names a representative `example_id` at `cut_index 0`, even when that specific row was never built - documented explicitly in the report. Traced against the `bad_call` fixture: this produces the exact error message and `example_id` the acceptance test (F3) expects, so it has no behavioral impact.
